newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - May fuel oil trades at $103/T.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - May fuel oil trades at $103/T.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps rose sharply at midday on Friday as fresh physical demand boosted prices to trade at well over the $100 mark, traders said.
"The market took off this morning after yesterday's physical trade which confirmed their perception that there's going to be a new round of buying," said a trader.
May fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $103.00/$104.00 per tonne, up from Thursday's $101.50/$102.50, brokers said.
May traded earlier in the day at $103.00, they said.
June swaps also put on a big gain and was last quoted at $102.00/$103.00, from Thursday's $99.50/$100.50, brokers said. June traded earlier in the day at $102.
Traders said prices rose after a local trader bought a 20,000 tonne cargo from a European major late Thursday at $102 per tonne for May 26-30 lifting, up $2 from Tuesday's traded level.
The swaps market was already expecting the fresh buying impetus and had rose by about $1.00 on Thursday following news of the arrival of a large cargo from the Gulf.

Firmer prices were also attributed to reduced exports from the Middle East due to high domestic summer demand and tight supplies from South Korea due to plant shutdowns for maintenance The market was also boosted by the 53 cent jump in overnight June Brent crude prices which closed at $18.69 per barrel.
The firmer crude market led to higher gas oil prices with May last quoted $25.45/$25.60 per barrel, up about 20 cents.
Brokers said May traded earlier in the day at $25.45 and $25.60 per barrel.
But June rose by about 30 cents to narrow the May/June spread further to value at about 30 cents from around 45 cents on Thursday.
